by Martin Coulter

Good morning Luca,



Over the past decade, Europe’s neobanks have burned through billions in VC money chasing growth.



Yet one neobank has quietly defied the playbook. Amsterdam-based Bunq is profitable, operates across Europe with a full banking licence and has amassed millions of users — all without raising VC funding.



But at home in the Netherlands, private equity-backed Bunq’s rise has been anything but low-profile. Dutch media have scrutinised its intense working culture, alongside allegations around lax financial crime controls and the misuse of customer data.



Former employees tell Sifted fintech reporter Tom Matsuda the company’s global ambitions have been undermined<https://email.sifted.eu/e3t/Ctc/LZ+113/d2mfCN04/MWYKGv_LG7XW96k5L08qmHltW2H1VMy5HmbL8N6Q02sq3qgz0W7Y8-PT6lZ3n1W62-YnB7455S7W2WGz1M8-gzCVW5MZptn938tTrW6pP3xH7T5DZmW19yqbv4BFkc8W2NPDsd1m2sCGW6Zbckl5R082gW19GLwf71jPhHW8K-Kkn8b-CvDW4CNcVb2Qh1J7W41DYF08BGdPVN81_wW9BlScRW2PvNz74lDlGQW1f4XVc1YtgN2W12mTH_3SLMqcN3hf-MP5g-DlN9629dTFbx_6W1tz2MZ1Zy7FNW6fWh4Q2dc2rHW2sHHHS6tpPLsW3n3Wn58tHwCcW1nF_2r80V1YqN3b3YwcPl6hRW83bX0l1PF7M2W2hzg373yc73rW2W4Kvj1nQPYvf6MG38x04> by shifting priorities and top-down decision-making. “You had to be at full speed every single minute of the day,” says one employee.



Questions over workplace culture, regulatory fines and legal battles now loom large, just as the neobank pushes into new markets like the US and eyes an eventual IPO.
